findings.title: Mobile layout has horizontal overflow in the top navigation and run history table
findings.description:
At a narrow mobile viewport, `/`, `/admin`, and `/run-history` became wider than the viewport instead of wrapping, collapsing, or containing overflow in an intentional scroller. The tester measured `document.documentElement.scrollWidth` at `600` while `clientWidth` was `375`, with top-nav links and run-history table columns beyond the right edge.

This was recorded as Low because mobile support was not part of the evaluated implementation scope, but it was not identified in GLM's self-audit.

findings.title: Public home mixes stale future-phase copy with a missing public custom/guardrail surface

relatedIndependentReviewFindings.note: Both findings identify the missing public custom/guardrail UI and stale placeholder presentation.

findings.description:
The public home page still described already-delivered surfaces as future work, including copy that said queue pressure, realtime events, ERP health, admin controls, ERP tuning, and reset would land in later phases. The `Surge Guardrails` panel also remained a placeholder (`Static placeholder surface - wired up in a later phase`) even though the roadmap/source review indicated `/` should expose bounded public custom/guardrail controls.

GLM's self-audit did identify a different public demo-picker problem, but it did not identify this stale-copy and public custom/guardrail surface gap.

findings.title: Admin run start accepts the run but does not move the operator to /watch
findings.description:
After signing in to `/admin`, selecting `Admin Custom (admin)`, and clicking `Start run`, the run became active and the start control was disabled, but the browser stayed on `/admin` instead of navigating the operator to `/watch`. Public starts from the home-page load-run control did navigate to `/watch`, so the admin flow remained inconsistent.

The self-audit caught a public-start redirect defect, but it did not identify this admin-start navigation gap.

findings.title: Live Watch can get stuck with partial run counters and a contradictory no-active-run completion panel

relatedIndependentReviewFindings.note: The browser reproduced contradictory stale panels; the code review identified incomplete recovery as a mechanism that leaves live panels stale.
The code review separately found that authoritative traffic metrics are ignored, contributing to partial and contradictory Watch projections.

findings.description:
After a public start navigated to `/watch`, the page showed live counters from the new run (`secured 62`, `queued 62`, `confirmed 62`, and inventory `938 of 1,000 remaining`) while the `Completion Outcomes` panel simultaneously said `No active run - completion outcomes appear once a run is in progress.` The contradictory state remained for at least 30 seconds, and `/run-history` later showed the same run as terminal `Failed`.

This is classified as a survived claimed fix because GLM's self-audit had already identified Live Watch state/recovery problems: `glm-5.2:F18` covered frozen recovery-sourced counts and missing terminal recovery refresh, while `glm-5.2:F16` covered Live Watch observing the wrong inventory target.

findings.title: Admin start control is enabled with no preset selected and fails silently
findings.description:
On signed-in `/admin`, the `Start run` button was enabled while the preset select still showed the placeholder `Select a preset...`. Clicking it produced no inline validation, toast, status change, or focus feedback.

This was not identified in GLM's self-audit.

findings.title: Repeated action buttons have indistinguishable accessible names
findings.description:
Several repeated controls exposed identical accessible button names without target-specific labels. Public preset cards and the separate load-run panel exposed multiple buttons named `Start load run`, and admin preset management exposed repeated `Duplicate` and `Copy to Custom` actions without target-specific accessible names.

This was not identified in GLM's self-audit.

findings.title: Failed runs do not expose an actionable explanation or detail view

relatedIndependentReviewFindings.note: Both findings identify the absence of a usable run-history detail surface; the browser report additionally emphasizes missing failure explanations.

findings.description:
Multiple non-idempotency runs finalized as `Failed` in `/run-history`, but the UI did not explain why. Rows showed high-level status, delivered counts, and outcome totals; outcome cards showed aggregate counts such as `CONFIRMED`, `FAILED`, `PROCESSING`, `QUEUED`, `ERP SUCCEEDED`, `ERP FAILED`, `ERP TIMED OUT`, and `NOTIFICATIONS`, but there was no visible detail route, expandable panel, or actionable failure explanation.

This makes the post-fix demo output hard to interpret because delivered orders can all be confirmed while the run status is still `Failed`. GLM's self-audit did not identify this run-history explanation/detail gap.
